title: aaif-goose/goose — an open source, extensible AI agent that goes beyond code suggestions - install, execute, edit, and test with any LLM
content:
your native open source AI agent — desktop app, CLI, and API — for code, workflows, and everything in between
goose is a general-purpose AI agent that runs on your machine. Not just for code — use it for research, writing, automation, data analysis, or anything you need to get done.
A native desktop app for macOS, Linux, and Windows. A full CLI for terminal workflows. An API to embed it anywhere. Built in Rust for performance and portability.
goose works with 15+ providers — Anthropic, OpenAI, Google, Ollama, OpenRouter, Azure, Bedrock, and more. Use API keys or your existing Claude, ChatGPT, or Gemini subscriptions via ACP. Connect to 70+ extensions via the Model Context Protocol open standard.
goose is part of the Agentic AI Foundation (AAIF) at the Linux Foundation.
Download the desktop app for macOS, Linux, and Windows.
Or install the CLI:
curl -fsSL https://github.com/aaif-goose/goose/releases/download/stable/download_cli.sh | bash

Because it always helps them "migrate" their code to production! 🚀

report.summary: Goose is a Rust-built, open source AI agent from the Linux Foundation's Agentic AI Foundation that runs locally across desktop, CLI, and API with 15+ LLM providers and 70+ MCP extensions.
report.background: AI coding tools spent 2023–2024 as autocomplete engines bolted onto editors. By 2025 the frontier shifted to agents that can read a repo, run commands, install dependencies, edit files, and execute tests in a loop until a task is done. That shift created two problems: lock-in, since most agents are tied to one vendor's model and one vendor's IDE, and trust, since autonomous execution means giving software shell access to your machine. Goose answers both by being fully open source, model-agnostic, and locally hosted, while leaning on the Model Context Protocol — an open standard Anthropic introduced and the wider ecosystem has since adopted — to plug into external tools. Its placement under the Agentic AI Foundation at the Linux Foundation signals a bid for neutral, vendor-independent governance, positioning it as the community counterweight to proprietary agents like Claude Code, Cursor, and Copilot Workspace.
key_points: One agent, three surfaces: a native desktop app for macOS, Linux, and Windows, a full CLI for terminal-centric workflows, and an embeddable API. The whole thing is written in Rust, which the project frames as a performance and portability choice — a single compiled binary rather than a Node or Python runtime stack.

Model freedom is the headline feature. Goose supports 15+ providers including Anthropic, OpenAI, Google, Ollama, OpenRouter, Azure, and Bedrock. Notably, it can reuse existing Claude, ChatGPT, or Gemini subscriptions via ACP, so users are not forced into per-token API billing to get started.

Extensibility runs through MCP. Over 70 extensions connect the agent to external systems, and because MCP is an open standard, third-party developers can publish new capabilities without waiting on the core team. The agent is designed to install, execute, edit, and test — not just suggest.

It is deliberately general-purpose rather than code-only. The project positions goose for research, writing, automation, and data analysis alongside software engineering, which broadens the addressable audience well beyond developers.

Governance and distribution are product features. Goose sits under the Agentic AI Foundation at the Linux Foundation, and it ships a Custom Distributions path so teams can build branded builds with preconfigured providers and extensions — an enterprise on-ramp that proprietary agents cannot easily match.
report.impact: For the AI industry, goose is a test of whether neutral, foundation-governed agents can compete with vendor-owned ones. If it works, MCP plus open governance becomes the default substrate and model providers compete on quality rather than distribution. For developers, the practical win is portability: swap models, run fully local via Ollama, embed the agent in CI or internal tooling through the API, and audit the code when it is about to touch production. For regular users, the desktop app lowers the barrier — an agent that handles research, writing, and automation without a terminal. The risk is unchanged: an agent with install and execute permissions is a real attack surface, so sandboxing and permission scoping matter more than the feature list.
report.tools: To go further, read the Model Context Protocol spec to understand how the 70+ extensions plug in. Compare with Cline (open source VS Code agent), Aider (terminal pair programmer), and OpenHands (formerly OpenDevin) for autonomous software tasks. Ollama enables fully local model runs; LiteLLM and OpenRouter simplify multi-provider routing. Continue covers IDE-native assistants. If you want to build your own distribution, study goose's Custom Distributions docs alongside MCP server SDKs in Python and TypeScript.
